title: A tokenizer for a tiny expression language
instructions:
## Characters in, tokens out

The lexer turns `total = price * 12 + 5` into a list of tokens. Write it by hand with an index into the string, the way generated lexers work underneath.

`tokenize(src)` returns a list of `(kind, text)` tuples with kinds: `NUMBER` (digits, optionally a dot and more digits), `IDENT` (a letter or underscore then letters, digits, underscores), `OP` (one of `+ - * / = ( )`), skipping spaces and tabs. Any other character raises `SyntaxError` with the message `unexpected character '<c>' at <index>`.

initialState.source:
def tokenize(src):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(src):
        c = src[i]
        # skip whitespace; read a number, an identifier or an operator; else raise
        i += 1
    return tokens


print(tokenize("total = price * 12 + 5"))

hints: if c.isdigit(): j = i; while j < len(src) and (src[j].isdigit() or src[j] == "."): j += 1; tokens.append(("NUMBER", src[i:j])); i = j; continue
Identifiers start with a letter or _ (c.isalpha() or c == "_") and continue with isalnum() or _.
raise SyntaxError(f"unexpected character {c!r} at {i}") for anything else.
realityNote: Tools such as flex and re2c generate this loop from regular expressions as a table-driven finite automaton. The error message with a position is what every later phase of the compiler relies on to point at the right place in the source.
